newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CLEMENS THROWS FIVE-HITTER AS JAYS ROUT RANGERS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CLEMENS THROWS FIVE-HITTER AS JAYS ROUT RANGERS.

text.p: Roger Clemens pitched a five-hitter for his major league-leading 15th win and Carlos Delgado homered twice and drove in five runs as the Toronto Blue Jays routed the Texas Rangers 9-1 Thursday.

Clemens (15-3), who beat Texas for the third time this season, walked three and struck out 10 to lower his ERA to 1.62, equalling Pedro Martinez of the Expos for the lowest in baseball. It was his fifth complete game of the year.
In three starts against the Rangers this season, the native Texan has allowed two runs and 11 hits over 23 innings with 20 strikeouts.
"The hitters deserve all the credit," Clemens said. "We've been waiting for them and it's good to see them have fun. I was fortunate to finish things off and give the bullpen some rest."
In his last three outings, Clemens has limited opponents to two runs and 13 hits over 26 innings with 36 strikeouts.
"Roger hasn't had a bad outing all year," said Toronto manager Cito Gaston. "We got some runs behind him and it gave him some breathing room."

Delgado hit a solo homer in the first off starter John Burkett (7-8) and added a three-run shot in the seventh off Xavier Hernandez. The five RBI matched a career high. Orlando Merced also homered for Toronto while Dean Palmer had a solo shot for Texas.
In Baltimore, Mo Vaughn's two-run homer in the top of the eighth off Jeese Orosco (2-2) snapped a tie and lifted the Boston Red Sox to a 12-9 victory over the Orioles.

Vaughn has torched the Orioles this season, hitting six homers in 12 games against them. He has 22 home runs this season and his 11 career round-trippers at Camden Yards tie him with Albert Belle for the most by a Baltimore opponent.
Vaughn was one of five Red Sox with at least three hits as Boston pounded out a season-high 21. John Valentin had four hits and is 17-for-39 since the All-Star break.
Ron Mahay (1-0), a former replacement player and converted outfielder, got his first major-league win, despite allowing one run in one inning.
Geronimo Berroa and Rafael Palmeiro homered for Baltimore.
In Chicago, David Cone (10-4) allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings and Wade Boggs had four hits to lead the New York Yankees to a 4-2 victory over the White Sox and a two-game sweep.
Cone gave up seven hits, walked one and struck out six.
Luis Sojo and Paul O'Neill each had two hits and scored a run for the Yankees, who moved within 3 1/2 games of first-place Baltimore in the American League East.

Mariano Rivera got his 30th save, equalling San Francisco's Rod Beck for the major-league lead. Rivera was helped by centre fielder Chad Curtis, who made a running catch at the wall on a one-out drive by Norberto Martin.
Danny Darwin (4-7) took the loss as the White Sox lost their fourth straight.

In Oakland, Matt Stairs drove in three runs for the second straight game and Steve Karsay posted his first home victory in nearly four years as the Athletics crushed the Kansas City Royals 11-3, tying a season high with their third straight win.

Stairs had an RBI single in the third, a sacrifice fly in the fourth and his 16th homer in the sixth. He is 9-for-15 in his last four games with four homers and 10 RBI, raising his average to .370. Jason Giambi and Scott Brosius homered in a six-run third inning for Oakland.
Karsay (3-9), plagued by injuries over the past three seasons, won at the Oakland Coliseum for the first time since August 1993, a span of 14 starts.
In Anaheim, Tony Phillips homered and drove in four runs and Luis Alicea added a triple and three RBI as the Angels won their 10th straight, defeating the Detroit Tigers 9-4.

Dennis Springer (5-3) allowed four runs and seven hits over seven innings, walking none -- for the first time in 18 starts this season -- and striking out five. He snapped a six-start winless drought.
The Tigers have lost six of their last eight.
In Milwaukee, Orel Hershiser (9-5) scattered two runs and four hits over six innings and Tony Fernandez had a two-run single in a three-run second as the Cleveland Indians edged the Brewers 3-2.
The Indians, who have won six of their last seven games, scored all their runs in the second off starter Cal Eldred (9-9).
In Seattle, Marty Cordova's opposite-field homer leading off the 12th inning against Norm Charltonlifted the Minnesota Twins to a 9-7 victory over the Mariners.
Charlton blew his eighth save of the season.
Chuck Knoblauch gave the Twins a brief lead with a one-out homer in the top of the 10th.

Rick Aguilera blew his second save opportunity in as many days by giving up an RBI single to Joey Cora in the 10th. But Aguilera (4-2) settled down and struck out the side in the 11th to get the win. Eddie Guardado got the save.
Scott Stahoviak and Rich Becker also homered for Minnesota. Alex Rodriguez homered for Seattle.
